A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same 3DThinker research. Their text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison. v1 ends after the references; v2 includes supplementary Sections 7–14, whose image-based prompts and case studies are readable.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, comparisons between training stages, ablations, and reconstructed point-cloud examples in Tables 1–6 and Figure 4.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical results and reports additional Qwen3-VL evaluations, benchmark comparisons, an alignment-loss ablation, training curves, and qualitative cases.

M1.justification: The two-stage framework, latent tokens, projector, and geometric alignment remain intact. Section 8.1 introduces a localized procedural adaptation: sequence-level GSPO replaces token-level GRPO for MoE models.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluated coverage on 3DSRBench (Table 9) and general image-understanding benchmarks MME, POPE, and SEED-I (Table 10). Section 8.3 explicitly extends the assessment to capabilities such as OCR and numerical reasoning, broadening the original spatial-reasoning evaluation.

E2.justification: Table 7 adds comparisons against five Qwen3-VL configurations, including the sparse 30B-A3B model. Table 9 newly compares against SpatialReasoner, SpatialReasoner-R1, and SpatialThinker. The LLaVA-OneVision-1.5 comparisons are retained unchanged in Table 8, having moved from v1's Table 1.

E3.justification: v2 adds dense/MoE Qwen3 configurations and a supervised alignment-loss-removal control. Section 3.1 also changes the reported CoT generator from GPT-4o to GPT-4.1. Existing accuracy/MRA metrics and MindCube hyperparameters remain unchanged; the newly disclosed curated-data settings do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds a supervised 3D-alignment-loss ablation (Table 11), a point-cloud-density analysis of prompt relevance (Section 8.4), training-curve analysis, and additional success and failure cases. These substantially extend the original latent-size, token-placement, projector, and reward ablations. Section 8.5 explains the existing projector comparison rather than introducing new ablation scores.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added training curves show optimization trajectories, not uncertainty across repeated experiments.

E6.justification: The original table scores, including the relocated LLaVA rows, are retained. New results include 80.8% MindCube-Tiny accuracy for 3DThinker on Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B (Table 7), 65.6 versus SpatialReasoner's 60.3 on 3DSRBench (Table 9), general-understanding scores, and 54.1 without alignment loss versus 62.7 with it (Table 11). These are newly reported results, not improvements to the retained v1 scores.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation in Equations 1–12 is unchanged. v2 adds no formal assumptions, propositions, proofs, or substantive derivations; the GSPO adaptation is described procedurally.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: intrinsic 3D latent reasoning without manual geometric labels or external inference priors, two-stage training, recoverable geometric representations, and effectiveness across VLM backbones. The additional experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: The supplement substantially expands interpretation and applicability boundaries. Section 11 clarifies annotation-free supervision and VGGT dependence; Section 8.6 interprets geometric supervision versus special-token flexibility; Section 14.2 links a failure to inconsistent reconstruction under extremely sparse views. It also discusses general-image capability retention and early RL exploration. The original non-autoregressive-latent and iterative-reasoning limitations are retained in Section 13.

D1.justification: v2 identifies the larger training corpus behind the unchanged, now-starred Table 2 results: 237K samples from four sources, Gemini quality filtering, one supervised epoch, and a 57K RL subset. It also supplies generation prompts, a ten-attempt regeneration rule, hardware, batch size, training times, and vLLM usage. The abstract changes code status from promised to available; this is a reported availability change, not externally verified access.

R1.justification: v2 adds four cited works: Adaptive Mixtures of Local Experts, DepthSSC, Swift Sampler, and Group Sequence Policy Optimization. The existing research positioning relative to textual cognitive maps, visual reasoning, and latent reasoning remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative receives limited grammatical edits, author/affiliation updates, and an acknowledgment. Existing limitations move from the conclusion to supplementary Section 13, and the supplement receives its own roadmap and sections. The main exposition is largely retained rather than extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the visual presentation with new result tables, density and projection illustrations, training plots, generation prompts, and detailed case-study panels. LLaVA rows move from Table 1 to Table 8, and Table 2 gains training-regime markers. Main Figures 1–4 retain the same images.

improvement.justification: v2 resolves an important reproducibility gap by identifying the substantially larger training corpus used for Table 2, which v1 did not distinguish from its MindCube training description. The new alignment-loss control, generation details, and explicit reconstruction failure substantially improve assessment of the method's support and limitations. Additional evaluations broaden that evidence. A new numerical inconsistency remains—Section 8.1 says 25.0 for Qwen3-VL-4B while Table 7 lists 26.0—but it is limited relative to these gains.
